# Attributed research adaptations

`trans_cmoeacd.py`, `trans_cmoeaaop.py`, `trans_cmoflcs.py`, `trans_ddpg.py` and relevant numerical kernels are Python problem adaptations of the corresponding PlatEMO algorithms at the pinned commit in `docs/experiments/trans_sources.json`.

Original source notice: Copyright (c) 2026 BIMK Group. Free use for research purposes. Publications using this platform or any platform code should acknowledge PlatEMO and cite Ye Tian, Ran Cheng, Xingyi Zhang, and Yaochu Jin, “PlatEMO: A MATLAB platform for evolutionary multi-objective optimization [educational forum],” IEEE Computational Intelligence Magazine, 2017, 12(4): 73–87. Cite each algorithm's own paper as well. This notice does not grant a broader license over upstream code.

The PSLGP-H-PD implementation draws on the algorithms in the Xu et al. paper and GP/brood settings in MengXu95/GPDFJSS-MENG. The repository's MIT license is retained in `GPDFJSS_MIT_LICENSE.txt` (Copyright 2016 Yi Mei). Its bundled ECJ sources also contain their own notices, including Academic Free License 3.0; raw sources retain those notices. We do not redistribute the Java runtime/library here. Newly written Python problem-adapter code does not imply ownership of the cited methods.

Paper PDFs are retained only as local research evidence and are not republished in this source tree. Retrieval manifest preserves upstream files unmodified. See `docs/experiments/trans_python.md` for material deviations; Python ports are not claims of bitwise MATLAB/Java equivalence or reproduction of published performance.
